reason: The cited evidence does not support the key premises: E2 shows amorphization in CoCrFeMnNi only under UHV sliding, not from carbon implantation, and E1 concerns a different alloy (AlCrTiZrMo) and deposition method, not plasma ion implantation. No evidence is provided for carbon-induced lubrication, annealing effects, or high-temperature performance of the proposed treatment.
premises: Carbon plasma ion implantation can induce amorphization and grain refinement in CoCrFeMnNi
An amorphous-carbon enriched surface layer can act as a solid lubricant and reduce friction
Post-implantation annealing promotes layer uniformity and adhesion
The treated layer remains effective from cryogenic temperatures up to ~800 °C
The untreated CoCrFeMnNi alloy has a friction coefficient of ~0.3
